text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to $150.80, capping a remarkable two-week surge of 12.45%. The catalyst is straightforward: oil prices have spiked sharply on Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $116 a barrel (a six-month high) after Saudi Arabia reported intercepting Houthi missiles and drones, while geopolitical rhetoric from the U.S. about potential action against Iran has kept supply concerns elevated. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices flow directly to the bottom line—more barrel revenue.

The broader tailwind here is that energy traders and analysts are now openly spotlighting oil stocks as a way to play the next leg of the energy trade, given how regional instability is reshaping global markets and benefiting U.S. energy companies. That shift in investor attention, combined with physical supply risk in one of the world's most critical regions, has created momentum that extends well beyond today's move.
